ui.seed_hint: Pick a seed, then tap a plot
ui.end_year_body: Winter starts at once. Ripe crops are reaped by the frost; growing ones wait for spring.
tip.0: Swipe across ripe crops to reap them all at once.
tip.1: Tap a crow to scare it off before it eats the crop.
tip.2: Tap on the beat: the halo tightens, and the strike hits two and a half times as hard.
tip.3: Crops keep growing and helpers keep working while you are away. Your stamina refills too.
tip.4: Passing the farm on earns seeds for stronger generations.
tip.5: In summer, tap the rain cloud to water the whole field.
tip.6: The seed bag lets you pick a crop for a bed; the best crop for it is marked.
tip.7: A ripe crop keeps its full price for a while, then slowly loses value until you pick it.
tip.8: A bed pays more when it grows something different from last year and from its neighbours.
tip.9: Tap the magnifier, then a bed, to see what it is worth right now and why.
tip.10: Scarecrows can be moved: tap one, then the corner it should stand on.
tip.11: No stamina? The swing still lands, just weaker. Reaping gives some back.
tip.12: The barn keeps part of every harvest for the winter market or for jars sold in spring.
tip.13: Settings can copy your farm as a code and load it on another phone.

help.title: How it works
help.crops.1: Each crop has a season it likes and pays more in. The seed bag says which, and lets you plant a cheaper crop on a good bed.
help.crops.2: A ripe crop keeps its full price for a while, then slowly loses value until it is picked. The magnifier on the field shows how fresh a bed is.
help.crops.3: A bed pays more when it grows something else than last year, and when the beds beside it grow something different again.
help.crops.4: Every reap sends the plot a layer deeper: tougher ground, richer coins. New ground from an expansion can be fertile and worth more.
help.year.1: A year runs spring, summer, autumn, then frost. Spring rain softens the ground, summer bakes it and slows growth, autumn pays swipes more.
help.year.2: The last ten seconds before frost pay extra on everything you pick.
help.year.3: At frost the year is graded on how fresh your harvests were: three stars pay the largest bonus. A yearly goal, when you meet it, pays on top.
help.winter.1: Winter opens the Almanac: coins buy nodes that stay for this generation. Nothing is spent by mistake — every node asks first.
help.winter.2: The barn keeps part of each harvest. In winter you sell it at that year's market price, or put it up as preserves, which pay more next spring.
help.winter.3: Once per generation you can undo the whole Almanac and get the coins back, if you want to build it differently.
help.heritage.1: When a generation has earned enough, you can hand the farm to the next one. Coins, the Almanac and the field go; Heritage Seeds stay.
help.heritage.2: Seeds buy Heritage nodes that every generation after keeps. Some pairs are either/or: taking one closes the other for good.
help.heritage.3: Each heir brings a trait, and you may take on a challenge generation, which makes the years harder and pays more seeds.
help.events.1: Crows land on ripe beds and eat them. Tap one to scare it off; a scarecrow, a dog or a hen keeps them away for you.
help.events.2: Moles, rabbits and locusts each cost you something different. A tap sends the first two off; strikes inside the swarm drive it away.
help.events.3: Storms, heat waves and fog change how the field works for a few seconds. A clover, a shooting star or a travelling trader is worth chasing.
help.away.1: The year clock stops when you close the game, so you never lose a year. Crops keep growing, your helpers and the tractor keep working for up to eight hours, and stamina refills.
help.away.2: The pause menu decides what the helpers do while you are gone: as they are, all harvesting, or half and half.
help.crop_line: {name} · tier {tier} · likes {season} · about {seconds} s from seed to ripe · {value} coins
help.crop_note: Times are unwatered at level one; holding triples them. The liked season pays a quarter more; deeper layers pay more still. Higher tiers need their Almanac node and a bed upgraded to match.

help.hoe.1: Tap hard ground to strike it. Every layer has a toughness; when it breaks, its coins come out and the seed drops by itself.
help.hoe.2: The field has a beat. A strike on the beat is a certain critical hit, two and a half times as hard. Off the beat you still have a chance.
help.hoe.3: Each strike costs stamina, which refills on its own and with every crop you reap. With none left the swing still lands, at less than half strength.
help.hoe.4: Hold a growing crop to water it: three times the growth while you hold. Swipe across ripe crops to reap them; more in one swipe pays more.
help.year.4: Winter keeps your depth and closes the cracks. What is ripe is reaped by the frost; what is growing waits for spring. Handing the farm on returns the field to the surface.
